sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The response that we were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt and G-d took us out is that through the Giving of the Torah, following the preparation of the Egyptian exile and exodus, the power was given to draw down the most sublime levels through practical mitzvos, and these drawn-downs would be in a state of revelation.

translations.translation: And the answer, "We were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt, and the L-rd took us out of Egypt," etc., is that through the Giving of the Torah, which was after the introduction of the exile of Egypt and the exodus from Egypt, the power was given that through practical mitzvos they would draw down the most sublime influences.
(As above in section 1),
and also that the influences through the performance of the mitzvos would be in revelation.
And this is, "And the L-rd commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear," etc.
"Fear" (yirah) is the letters of "seeing" (re'iyah).
(As explained in the maamar47),
that the influences through the performance of the mitzvos
("And He commanded us... to do")
will be in revelation, to the level of seeing.
And the main revelation of the influences through the performance of the mitzvos will be in the Future to Come,
for then there will be seeing at the most sublime levels,
and up to "fear"
(the letters of "seeing")
"the L-rd our G-d,"
the seeing of the essence of Ein Sof, blessed be He48.
And this is, "And the L-rd commanded us to do all these statutes," etc.,
specifically "statutes" (chukim),
for when one fulfills the mitzvos
(only)
because of the reason,
the influences through the mitzvos are in concealment49,
and in order for the influences of the mitzvos to be in revelation,
it is through the fulfillment of the mitzvos
(even the mitzvos of testimonies and laws)
being because they are the command of G-d,
like the statutes50.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Since the Torah calls him a wise son, he knows the innovation of the Giving of the Torah, yet his question is explained by the fact that the Giving of the Torah occurs daily, requiring a new level of service each day akin to the service of the Patriarchs before the Giving of the Torah.

translations.translation: Now, after all the above, explanation is needed,
for since the Torah of Truth calls him by the name
("son")
wise,
it is logical
that he knows the innovation of the Giving of the Torah,
that through the Giving of the Torah the power was given to draw down through practical mitzvos the most sublime influences and that the influences would be in revelation,
so what is the question, "What are these testimonies," etc.?
And this can be explained based on what is stated elsewhere51,
that the fact that the deeds of the Patriarchs are related in the Torah
(even though the service of the Patriarchs was seemingly only a preparation for the Giving of the Torah),
is
because even now, after the Giving of the Torah, there must be service similar to the service of the Patriarchs.
And the concept is,
that we are commanded, "Each and every day they shall be in your eyes
(as new ones52,
and even more so)
new53,"
this is not only regarding the preciousness and endearment of Torah and mitzvos,
but also regarding the study of Torah and the fulfillment of the mitzvos themselves.
That each day one must be on an even higher level,
as the command54
"We ascend in holiness,"
and up to an incomparable ascent,
and to the point that the Torah and mitzvos that he had previously are
(as if they were of no account, or)
of no account compared to the Torah and mitzvos of this day,
therefore the Torah and mitzvos of this day are
(as new ones, or)
new.
And this is that even now, after the Giving of the Torah, there must be service similar to the service of the Patriarchs before the Giving of the Torah,
for the Giving of the Torah is every day,
"the Giver of the Torah" is in the present tense55,
and each day it is on a higher level,
therefore,
each day there must be service similar to the service of the Patriarchs, which is preparation and introduction for the Giving of the Torah of this day.
And based on this, the question of the wise son, "What are these testimonies... which the L-rd our G-d commanded you," can be explained,
for the Torah and mitzvos of the wise son are truly new each day,
and therefore he is always at his beginning, in the state before the Giving of the Torah.
And it can be said,
that what he says, "which the L-rd commanded you,"
"you" and not "us,"
is
in order to hint that with him it is the state before the Giving of the Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The wise son's question is primarily on Passover night because Passover is the birth of the Jewish people, and he is in a state before the Giving of the Torah, like a newborn who is not yet connected to anything.

translations.translation: And 4)
And this can be connected with the fact that the question of the wise son is primarily on the night of Passover,
even though the question, "What are these testimonies," etc.
(simply)
is regarding all the mitzvos,
for on Passover is the birth of the Jewish people56.
And this is that the holiday of Passover is particularly connected to the matter of education,
for the education of children begins immediately when one is born.
And this is the connection of the wise son's question with the night of Passover,
for that he asks, "What are these testimonies," etc., is because
(from the aspect that he constantly ascends from one level to another)
he is in a state before the Giving of the Torah,
and that he is not yet connected to any matter,
like an infant at the moment of birth.
